title: Batch orchestration and KV residency recalibration for mixed-length dialogs
creator: Avery Chen
description: Background: We've seen production workloads with highly mixed prompt and response lengths (chat customers, multi-turn assistants) causing recurring GPU memory pressure and tail-latency spikes. Existing continuous-batcher heuristics prioritize fill-rate and sequence-length buckets, but KV residency (how long KV cache segments persist) and prefetch eviction timing are not coordinated with slot coalescing. This ticket proposes restructuring the batching orchestration to decouple transient short exchanges from long-horizon responses via a KV residency recalibration layer.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce a KV residency policy that classifies requests into three residency classes (ephemeral: short prompt + short response, persistent: long response or streaming, hybrid: short prompt + expected long response) and enforces adaptive TTLs on KV segments. 2) Extend the scheduler to tag incoming requests with a residency hint computed from sequence histogram, user-provided hints, and recent request history. 3) Use residency tags to control slot coalescing windows: ephemeral slots allow aggressive coalescing (higher pack density), persistent slots reserve dedicated KV slabs with compaction-friendly GC, hybrid slots default to conservative coalescing and early prefetch. 4) Add a GPU-slab compaction pass that runs during low-util windows to defragment KV memory and reclaim fragmented slabs belonging to persistent workloads.
acceptance_criteria:
- No regression in 99th percentile latency for 95% of customer clusters during a 72-hour A/B test.
- At least 18% reduction in KV-induced OOM incidents on the test fleet against baseline over a 7-day run.
- Token throughput per-GPU improves or stays within 3% of baseline for mixed-length workloads.
- New metrics appear in Console: residency_distribution, kv_ttl_evictions, slab_fragmentation_index.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for residency tagger and TTL assignment logic.
- Integration test that simulates mixed-length dialog traces (synth + replay of anonymized traces) to validate slot coalescing behavior.
- Canary rollout on dedicated staging cluster (dev-dedicated-5) with traffic mirroring.
- Rollback criteria: >5% increase in tail-latency or any OOM on production hosts.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Feature flag behind 'kv_residency_v2' and enable on 10% of non-critical customer traffic. Phase 2: Expand to internal dedicated clusters and run extended soak. Phase 3: Gradually increase to 100% after 72-hour stability window and confirm metrics.
Post-rollout: schedule a maintenance compaction window and surface compaction logs to Console.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Misclassification risk: wrong residency hint could worsen latency. Mitigation: conservative defaults and a per-request fallback to baseline packing.
- Compaction cost: background compaction might compete for GPU memory. Mitigation: throttle compaction during high-U and move compaction to underutilized devices or maintenance windows.
- Customer regressions for latency-sensitive tenants. Mitigation: start with non-SLA customer cohorts and allow per-tenant opt-out.
open_questions: What is the cost model for keeping persistent KV slabs pinned on multi-tenant GPUs?
Should we allow customers to provide explicit residency hints via API headers for high-confidence use cases?
What is the best heuristic for transitioning a hybrid request to persistent mid-stream if the response expands beyond expectations?
